thought.text: I copied the script to the old container before deleting it. Let me copy it to the new one.

reasoning_content: docker cp was executed against a stopped/deleted container, or the cp failed because it was done before the rm. Actually I did cp and then rm'd the container. `docker cp` to a running container should work, but it displayed that the file doesn't exist — because docker cp to a running container places the file on the container's filesystem, and that should persist... no wait, the issue is: I copied to smtp-sink and then immediately ran `docker rm -f smtp-sink`, so the copied file got deleted along with the container. Then I started a new container. I need to either copy to the new container or use a different approach. Let me either copy it into the new container, or mount the file and use it.

action.command:
docker cp /tmp/sink.py smtp-sink:/sink.py
docker restart smtp-sink
sleep 5
docker logs smtp-sink 2>&1 | grep -vE "Deprecat|import asyn" 
echo "--- trigger login ---"
docker exec workspace-postgres-1 psql -U daz -d daz -c "DELETE FROM email_otps;" >/dev/null
docker run --rm --network workspace_default curlimages/curl:latest -sS -X POST http://backend:4000/api/v1/auth/init-email-login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"client":"dashboard","emailAddress":"admin@schule.de","schoolSlug":"eckener-schule"}' -w "\nHTTP:%{http_code}\n"
sleep 6
echo "--- mail.log ---"
docker exec smtp-sink sh -c 'cat /mail.log 2>/dev/null | head -40 || echo "(no mail yet)"'
